questions.stem: A car travels at \(40\) km/hr for the first half of its journey and at \(60\) km/hr for the second half. If the total distance is \(200\) km, what is the total time taken?
questions.keySolution:
First half distance = \(100\) km at \(40\) km/hr
Time for first half = \(100/40 = 2.5\) hours
Second half distance = \(100\) km at \(60\) km/hr
Time for second half = \(100/60 = 5/3\) hours = \(1\) hour \(40\) minutes
Total time = \(2.5 + 5/3 = 2.5 + 1.67 = 4.17\) hours = \(4\) hours \(10\) minutes

questions.stem: A train increases its speed by \(20\%\) and covers \(240\) km in \(3\) hours. What was its original speed?
questions.keySolution:
New speed after \(20\%\) increase = \(240/3 = 80\) km/hr
Let original speed = \(x\) km/hr
New speed = \(x + 0.20x = 1.20x\)
\(1.20x = 80\)
\(x = 80/1.20 = 66.67\) km/hr

questions.stem: A person walks at \(4\) km/hr for \(2\) hours, then increases speed to \(6\) km/hr for the next \(3\) hours. What is the average speed for the entire journey?
questions.keySolution:
Distance in first \(2\) hours = \(4 × 2 = 8\) km
Distance in next \(3\) hours = \(6 × 3 = 18\) km
Total distance = \(8 + 18 = 26\) km
Total time = \(2 + 3 = 5\) hours
Average speed = \(26/5 = 5.2\) km/hr

questions.stem: If a cyclist reduces his speed by \(25\%\), he takes \(2\) hours more to cover a certain distance. What is his usual time to cover that distance?
questions.keySolution:
Let usual time = \(t\) hours and usual speed = \(v\) km/hr
Reduced speed = \(0.75v\)
New time = \(t + 2\)
Distance remains same: \(vt = 0.75v(t + 2)\)
\(t = 0.75(t + 2)\)
\(t = 0.75t + 1.5\)
\(0.25t = 1.5\)
\(t = 6\) hours

questions.stem: A bus travels \(150\) km at \(50\) km/hr, then \(200\) km at \(40\) km/hr. What is the average speed for the entire journey?
questions.keySolution:
Time for first part = \(150/50 = 3\) hours
Time for second part = \(200/40 = 5\) hours
Total distance = \(150 + 200 = 350\) km
Total time = \(3 + 5 = 8\) hours
Average speed = \(350/8 = 43.75\) km/hr

questions.stem: A man drives at \(60\) km/hr for \(3\) hours, then increases speed by \(50\%\) for the next \(2\) hours. What is the total distance covered?
questions.keySolution:
Distance in first \(3\) hours = \(60 × 3 = 180\) km
Increased speed = \(60 + 50\% \text{ of } 60 = 60 + 30 = 90\) km/hr
Distance in next \(2\) hours = \(90 × 2 = 180\) km
Total distance = \(180 + 180 = 360\) km

questions.stem: If a car's speed is increased by \(10\%\), the time taken to travel a certain distance decreases by what percentage?
questions.keySolution:
Let original speed = \(100\) units, time = \(100\) units
New speed = \(110\) units
New time = \(100 × 100/110 = 10000/110 = 90.91\) units
Decrease in time = \(100 - 90.91 = 9.09\) units
Percentage decrease = \(9.09\%\)

questions.stem: A train running at \(72\) km/hr takes \(5\) seconds to cross a pole. If it reduces its speed to \(54\) km/hr, how much time will it take to cross the same pole?
A person covers \(1/3\) of distance at \(30\) km/hr, \(1/3\) at \(40\) km/hr and remaining at \(60\) km/hr. What is the average speed?
questions.keySolution:
Let total distance = \(3d\)
Time for first part = \(d/30\)
Time for second part = \(d/40\)
Time for third part = \(d/60\)
Total time = \(d(1/30 + 1/40 + 1/60) = d(4 + 3 + 2)/120 = 9d/120\)
Average speed = \(3d ÷ (9d/120) = 3d × 120/(9d) = 360/9 = 40\) km/hr

questions.stem: A motorist travels \(200\) km at \(80\) km/hr and returns at \(120\) km/hr. What is his average speed for the round trip?
questions.keySolution:
Time for onward journey = \(200/80 = 2.5\) hours
Time for return journey = \(200/120 = 5/3\) hours
Total distance = \(200 + 200 = 400\) km
Total time = \(2.5 + 5/3 = 2.5 + 1.67 = 4.17\) hours
Average speed = \(400/4.17 = 96\) km/hr

questions.stem: If walking at \(6/5\) of his usual speed, a man reaches \(10\) minutes early. What is his usual time?
questions.keySolution:
Let usual time = \(t\) minutes
New speed = \(6/5\) of usual speed
New time = \(t × 5/6\)
Time saved = \(t - t × 5/6 = t/6 = 10\) minutes
Therefore, \(t = 60\) minutes

questions.stem: A car travels at \(45\) km/hr for \(4\) hours, then at \(60\) km/hr for \(3\) hours, and finally at \(30\) km/hr for \(2\) hours. What is the average speed?
questions.keySolution:
Distance covered in \(4\) hours = \(45 × 4 = 180\) km
Distance covered in \(3\) hours = \(60 × 3 = 180\) km
Distance covered in \(2\) hours = \(30 × 2 = 60\) km
Total distance = \(180 + 180 + 60 = 420\) km
Total time = \(4 + 3 + 2 = 9\) hours
Average speed = \(420/9 = 46.67 ≈ 47\) km/hr

questions.stem: A train's speed is reduced by \(15\%\) due to fog. If it now takes \(20\) minutes more to cover \(68\) km, what was the original speed?
questions.keySolution:
Let original speed = \(v\) km/hr
Reduced speed = \(0.85v\) km/hr
Original time = \(68/v\) hours
New time = \(68/(0.85v)\) hours
Difference = \(68/(0.85v) - 68/v = 20/60 = 1/3\) hours
\(68(1/0.85v - 1/v) = 1/3\)
\(68 × 0.15/(0.85v) = 1/3\)
\(v = 60\) km/hr

questions.stem: A cyclist covers \(20\) km at \(16\) km/hr and \(30\) km at \(24\) km/hr. What is his average speed?
questions.keySolution:
Time for first \(20\) km = \(20/16 = 1.25\) hours
Time for next \(30\) km = \(30/24 = 1.25\) hours
Total distance = \(20 + 30 = 50\) km
Total time = \(1.25 + 1.25 = 2.5\) hours
Average speed = \(50/2.5 = 20\) km/hr

questions.stem: A man increases his speed by \(25\%\) and covers a distance \(15\) minutes earlier than usual. What is his usual time?
questions.keySolution:
Let usual time = \(t\) minutes
New speed = \(1.25\) times usual speed
New time = \(t/1.25 = 0.8t\)
Time saved = \(t - 0.8t = 0.2t = 15\) minutes
Therefore, \(t = 15/0.2 = 75\) minutes

questions.stem: A bus covers \(100\) km in \(2.5\) hours at constant speed. If it increases speed by \(20\%\), how much time will it take to cover \(120\) km?
questions.keySolution:
Original speed = \(100/2.5 = 40\) km/hr
New speed = \(40 + 20\% \text{ of } 40 = 40 + 8 = 48\) km/hr
Time for \(120\) km = \(120/48 = 2.5\) hours

questions.stem: A person drives \(28\) km/hr for \(2.5\) hours, then increases speed by \(28\) km/hr and reaches destination in \(1\) hour. What is the average speed?
questions.keySolution:
Distance in first part = \(28 × 2.5 = 70\) km
Speed in second part = \(28 + 28 = 56\) km/hr
Distance in second part = \(56 × 1 = 56\) km
Total distance = \(70 + 56 = 126\) km
Total time = \(2.5 + 1 = 3.5\) hours
Average speed = \(126/3.5 = 36\) km/hr

questions.stem: A train decreases its speed from \(90\) km/hr to \(60\) km/hr. By what percentage does the time increase for covering the same distance?
questions.keySolution:
Let distance = \(180\) km (LCM of \(90\) and \(60\))
Original time = \(180/90 = 2\) hours
New time = \(180/60 = 3\) hours
Increase in time = \(3 - 2 = 1\) hour
Percentage increase = \((1/2) × 100 = 50\%\)

questions.stem: A car travels \(240\) km. For the first \(120\) km, it travels at \(60\) km/hr and for the remaining distance at \(80\) km/hr. What is the average speed?
questions.keySolution:
Time for first \(120\) km = \(120/60 = 2\) hours
Time for remaining \(120\) km = \(120/80 = 1.5\) hours
Total time = \(2 + 1.5 = 3.5\) hours
Average speed = \(240/3.5 = 68.57\) km/hr

questions.stem: If a runner increases his speed by \(40\%\), he takes \(15\) minutes less to complete a race. What is his original time?
questions.keySolution:
Let original time = \(t\) minutes
New speed = \(1.4\) times original speed
New time = \(t/1.4\)
Time saved = \(t - t/1.4 = t(1 - 1/1.4) = t × 0.4/1.4 = 15\)
\(t = 15 × 1.4/0.4 = 37.5\) minutes

questions.stem: A vehicle covers \(80\) km at \(40\) km/hr and next \(80\) km at \(60\) km/hr. What is the average speed for the entire journey?
questions.keySolution:
Time for first \(80\) km = \(80/40 = 2\) hours
Time for next \(80\) km = \(80/60 = 4/3\) hours
Total distance = \(80 + 80 = 160\) km
Total time = \(2 + 4/3 = 10/3\) hours
Average speed = \(160 ÷ 10/3 = 160 × 3/10 = 48\) km/hr

questions.stem: A train running at \(108\) km/hr crosses a platform in \(15\) seconds. If it reduces speed to \(72\) km/hr, how much time will it take to cross the same platform?
A man covers half the distance at \(x\) km/hr and remaining half at \(y\) km/hr. What is his average speed?
questions.keySolution:
Let total distance = \(2d\)
Time for first half = \(d/x\)
Time for second half = \(d/y\)
Total time = \(d/x + d/y = d(x + y)/(xy)\)
Average speed = \(2d ÷ d(x + y)/(xy) = 2xy/(x + y)\)

questions.stem: If speed is decreased by \(30\%\), by what percentage should time be increased to cover the same distance?
questions.keySolution:
New speed = \(70\%\) of original speed = \(0.7s\)
For same distance: \(s × t = 0.7s × T\)
\(T = t/0.7 = 10t/7\)
Increase in time = \(10t/7 - t = 3t/7\)
Percentage increase = \((3t/7)/t × 100 = 3/7 × 100 = 42.86\%\)

questions.stem: A cyclist travels \(60\) km at \(20\) km/hr, then \(40\) km at \(10\) km/hr. What is the average speed?
questions.keySolution:
Time for first \(60\) km = \(60/20 = 3\) hours
Time for next \(40\) km = \(40/10 = 4\) hours
Total distance = \(60 + 40 = 100\) km
Total time = \(3 + 4 = 7\) hours
Average speed = \(100/7 = 14.29\) km/hr

questions.stem: A train increases its speed by \(25\%\) after covering \(200\) km in \(4\) hours. What is the new speed?
questions.keySolution:
Original speed = \(200/4 = 50\) km/hr
Increase = \(25\%\) of \(50 = 12.5\) km/hr
New speed = \(50 + 12.5 = 62.5\) km/hr

questions.stem: A person walks \(1/4\) of the way at \(3\) km/hr, \(1/2\) of the way at \(4\) km/hr and remaining at \(6\) km/hr. Find average speed.
questions.keySolution:
Let total distance = \(12d\) (LCM of \(4, 2, 4\))
Time for \(3d\) at \(3\) km/hr = \(3d/3 = d\)
Time for \(6d\) at \(4\) km/hr = \(6d/4 = 1.5d\)
Time for \(3d\) at \(6\) km/hr = \(3d/6 = 0.5d\)
Total time = \(d + 1.5d + 0.5d = 3d\)
Average speed = \(12d/3d = 4\) km/hr

questions.stem: A bus reduces its speed by \(20\%\) and takes \(30\) minutes more to travel \(120\) km. What was the original speed?
questions.keySolution:
Let original speed = \(v\) km/hr
New speed = \(0.8v\) km/hr
Original time = \(120/v\) hours
New time = \(120/(0.8v) = 150/v\) hours
Difference = \(150/v - 120/v = 30/v = 0.5\) hours
\(v = 30/0.5 = 60\) km/hr

questions.stem: A car covers first \(100\) km at \(50\) km/hr and next \(150\) km at \(60\) km/hr. What is the average speed?
questions.keySolution:
Time for first \(100\) km = \(100/50 = 2\) hours
Time for next \(150\) km = \(150/60 = 2.5\) hours
Total distance = \(100 + 150 = 250\) km
Total time = \(2 + 2.5 = 4.5\) hours
Average speed = \(250/4.5 = 55.56\) km/hr

questions.stem: If a man doubles his speed, he reaches \(30\) minutes earlier. What is his usual time?
questions.keySolution:
Let usual time = \(t\) minutes
When speed doubles, time becomes \(t/2\)
Time saved = \(t - t/2 = t/2 = 30\) minutes
Therefore, \(t = 60\) minutes

questions.stem: A train running at \(60\) km/hr takes \(10\) seconds to cross a bridge. If it increases speed to \(80\) km/hr, how much time will it take?

questions.stem: A motorcycle covers \(150\) km in \(3\) hours. If it increases speed by \(10\) km/hr, how much time will it save for the same distance?
questions.keySolution:
Original speed = \(150/3 = 50\) km/hr
New speed = \(50 + 10 = 60\) km/hr
New time = \(150/60 = 2.5\) hours
Time saved = \(3 - 2.5 = 0.5\) hours = \(30\) minutes

questions.stem: A train travels \(300\) km at \(75\) km/hr, then \(200\) km at \(50\) km/hr. What is the average speed?
questions.keySolution:
Time for first \(300\) km = \(300/75 = 4\) hours
Time for next \(200\) km = \(200/50 = 4\) hours
Total distance = \(300 + 200 = 500\) km
Total time = \(4 + 4 = 8\) hours
Average speed = \(500/8 = 62.5\) km/hr

questions.stem: If speed is increased by \(20\%\), time decreases by what percentage for covering same distance?
questions.keySolution:
New speed = \(1.2\) times original speed
New time = Original time \(÷ 1.2 = \frac{5}{6}\) of original time
Decrease = Original time \(- \frac{5}{6}\) original time \(= \frac{1}{6}\) original time
Percentage decrease = \(\frac{1/6}{1} × 100 = 16.67\%\)

questions.stem: A bus covers \(90\) km at \(45\) km/hr and returns at \(30\) km/hr. What is the average speed for round trip?
questions.keySolution:
Time for onward journey = \(90/45 = 2\) hours
Time for return journey = \(90/30 = 3\) hours
Total distance = \(90 + 90 = 180\) km
Total time = \(2 + 3 = 5\) hours
Average speed = \(180/5 = 36\) km/hr

questions.stem: A person runs at \(8\) km/hr for first \(1\) km, then at \(6\) km/hr for next \(2\) km, and finally at \(4\) km/hr for last \(1\) km. Find average speed.
questions.keySolution:
Time for first \(1\) km = \(1/8 = 0.125\) hours
Time for next \(2\) km = \(2/6 = 1/3 = 0.333\) hours
Time for last \(1\) km = \(1/4 = 0.25\) hours
Total distance = \(1 + 2 + 1 = 4\) km
Total time = \(0.125 + 0.333 + 0.25 = 0.708\) hours
Average speed = \(4/0.708 = 5.65 ≈ 5.71\) km/hr

questions.stem: A train decreases speed from \(80\) km/hr to \(64\) km/hr. What is the percentage decrease in speed?
questions.keySolution:
Decrease in speed = \(80 - 64 = 16\) km/hr
Percentage decrease = \((16/80) × 100 = 20\%\)

questions.stem: A car travels for \(2\) hours at \(50\) km/hr, then for \(3\) hours at \(40\) km/hr, and finally for \(1\) hour at \(60\) km/hr. What is the average speed?
questions.keySolution:
Distance in \(2\) hours = \(50 × 2 = 100\) km
Distance in \(3\) hours = \(40 × 3 = 120\) km
Distance in \(1\) hour = \(60 × 1 = 60\) km
Total distance = \(100 + 120 + 60 = 280\) km
Total time = \(2 + 3 + 1 = 6\) hours
Average speed = \(280/6 = 46.67\) km/hr

questions.stem: A cyclist covers a distance in \(4\) hours at \(15\) km/hr. If he increases speed by \(33.33\%\), how much time will he save?
questions.keySolution:
Distance = \(15 × 4 = 60\) km
New speed = \(15 + 33.33\% \text{ of } 15 = 15 + 5 = 20\) km/hr
New time = \(60/20 = 3\) hours
Time saved = \(4 - 3 = 1\) hour

questions.stem: A train covers \(180\) km at \(60\) km/hr and next \(120\) km at \(40\) km/hr. What is the average speed?
questions.keySolution:
Time for \(180\) km = \(180/60 = 3\) hours
Time for \(120\) km = \(120/40 = 3\) hours
Total distance = \(180 + 120 = 300\) km
Total time = \(3 + 3 = 6\) hours
Average speed = \(300/6 = 50\) km/hr

questions.stem: If a person increases his speed by \(60\%\), he reaches \(20\) minutes earlier. What was his original time?
questions.keySolution:
Let original time = \(t\) minutes
New speed = \(1.6\) times original speed
New time = \(t/1.6 = 5t/8\)
Time saved = \(t - 5t/8 = 3t/8 = 20\) minutes
\(t = 20 × 8/3 = 160/3 = 53.33 ≈ 50\) minutes

questions.stem: A vehicle travels \(240\) km. First \(80\) km at \(40\) km/hr, next \(80\) km at \(60\) km/hr, and last \(80\) km at \(80\) km/hr. Find average speed.
questions.keySolution:
Time for first \(80\) km = \(80/40 = 2\) hours
Time for second \(80\) km = \(80/60 = 4/3 = 1.33\) hours
Time for third \(80\) km = \(80/80 = 1\) hour
Total time = \(2 + 1.33 + 1 = 4.33\) hours
Average speed = \(240/4.33 = 55.43 ≈ 54.55\) km/hr

questions.stem: A runner completes first half of race at \(12\) km/hr and second half at \(18\) km/hr. What is his average speed?
questions.keySolution:
Let each half distance = \(d\)
Time for first half = \(d/12\)
Time for second half = \(d/18\)
Total time = \(d/12 + d/18 = d(18 + 12)/(12 × 18) = 30d/216 = 5d/36\)
Average speed = \(2d ÷ (5d/36) = 2d × 36/(5d) = 72/5 = 14.4\) km/hr

questions.stem: A car's speed is reduced by \(10\%\). By what percentage does the time increase for same distance?
questions.keySolution:
New speed = \(90\%\) of original = \(0.9s\)
New time = \(d/(0.9s) = d/s ÷ 0.9 = t/0.9\)
Increase in time = \(t/0.9 - t = t(1/0.9 - 1) = t × 0.1/0.9 = t/9\)
Percentage increase = \((t/9)/t × 100 = 100/9 = 11.11\%\)

questions.stem: A person covers \(60\) km at \(30\) km/hr and \(40\) km at \(20\) km/hr. What is the average speed?
questions.keySolution:
Time for \(60\) km = \(60/30 = 2\) hours
Time for \(40\) km = \(40/20 = 2\) hours
Total distance = \(60 + 40 = 100\) km
Total time = \(2 + 2 = 4\) hours
Average speed = \(100/4 = 25\) km/hr

questions.stem: A train increases its speed from \(40\) km/hr to \(60\) km/hr. What is the percentage increase?
questions.keySolution:
Increase in speed = \(60 - 40 = 20\) km/hr
Percentage increase = \((20/40) × 100 = 50\%\)

questions.stem: A motorcycle covers \(120\) km at variable speeds. First \(40\) km at \(20\) km/hr, next \(40\) km at \(30\) km/hr, last \(40\) km at \(60\) km/hr. Find average speed.
questions.keySolution:
Time for first \(40\) km = \(40/20 = 2\) hours
Time for second \(40\) km = \(40/30 = 4/3 = 1.33\) hours
Time for third \(40\) km = \(40/60 = 2/3 = 0.67\) hours
Total time = \(2 + 1.33 + 0.67 = 4\) hours
Average speed = \(120/4 = 30\) km/hr
